newsitem.title: USA: Ametek seeks consent of noteholders in deal.
newsitem.headline: Ametek seeks consent of noteholders in deal.

text.p: AMETEK Inc said Friday that it will offer a consent payment of $3.75 per $1,000 to holders of its 9.75 percent senior notes, in connection with the sale of its water filitration business to Culligan Water Technologies Inc.
The offer, open to shareholder of record May 15, closes May 30. The company said that there are $150 million of the notes, due 2004, outstanding.
The spin-off to Culligan, for 3.5 million shares, utilizes a "Morris" trust structure, a method that allows the deal to proceed on a tax-free basis.

The company said that the indenture agreement did not contemplate such an action, and that it was seeking the noteholders consent to clarify any ambiguities that might occur. AMETEK, however, said it believes the consummation of the Culligan transaction will not conflict with the terms of the indenture.
The company said that the right to receive payment is contingent upon receiving consents from the holders of a majority of the total principal of the notes.
